In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] field of [[general topology]], a '''Dowker space''' is a [[topological space]] that is [[normal space|T<sub>4</sub>]] but not [[paracompact space|countably paracompact]]. They are named after [[Clifford Hugh Dowker]].

The non-trivial task of providing an example of a Dowker space (and therefore also proving their existence as mathematical objects) helped mathematicians better understand the nature and variety of [[topological space]]s.

==Equivalences==
Dowker showed, in 1951, the following:

If ''X'' is a normal [[T1 space|T<sub>1</sub> space]] (that is, a [[T4 space|T<sub>4</sub> space]]), then the following are equivalent:
* ''X'' is a Dowker space
* The product of ''X'' with the unit interval is not normal.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Dowker |first=C. H. |authorlink=Clifford Hugh Dowker |date=1951 |title=On countably paracompact spaces |journal=[[Canadian Journal of Mathematics|Can. J. Math.]] |volume=3 |pages=219–224 |doi=10.4153/CJM-1951-026-2 |zbl=0042.41007 |url=http://cms.math.ca/cjm/v3/cjm1951v03.0219-0224.pdf |accessdate=March 29, 2015 |archive-date=July 14, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714144135/http://cms.math.ca/cjm/v3/cjm1951v03.0219-0224.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* ''X'' is not [[Metacompact space|countably metacompact]].

Dowker conjectured that there were no Dowker spaces, and the conjecture was not resolved until [[Mary Ellen Rudin]] constructed one in 1971.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Rudin |first=Mary Ellen |authorlink=Mary Ellen Rudin |date=1971 |title=A normal space ''X'' for which ''X &times; I'' is not normal |journal=[[Fundamenta Mathematicae|Fundam. Math.]] |publisher=Polish Academy of Sciences |volume=73 |number=2 |pages=179–186 |doi=10.4064/fm-73-2-179-186 |zbl=0224.54019 |url=http://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/fm/fm73/fm73121.pdf |accessdate=March 29, 2015}}</ref> Rudin's counterexample is a very large space (of [[cardinality]] <math>\aleph_\omega^{\aleph_0}</math>). [[Zoltán Tibor Balogh|Zoltán Balogh]] gave the first [[ZFC]] construction of a small (cardinality [[Cardinality of the continuum|continuum]]) example,<ref>{{cite journal |last=Balogh |first=Zoltan T. |authorlink=Zoltán Tibor Balogh |date=August 1996 |title=A small Dowker space in ZFC |journal=[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society|Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.]] |volume=124 |number=8 |pages=2555–2560 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-96-03610-6 |zbl=0876.54016 |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/proc/1996-124-08/S0002-9939-96-03610-6/S0002-9939-96-03610-6.pdf |accessdate=March 29, 2015}}</ref> which was more [[well-behaved]] than Rudin's. Using [[PCF theory]], M. Kojman and [[Saharon Shelah|S. Shelah]] constructed a subspace of Rudin's Dowker space of cardinality <math>\aleph_{\omega+1}</math> that is also Dowker.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kojman |first1=Menachem |last2=Shelah |first2=Saharon |authorlink2=Saharon Shelah |date=1998 |title=A ZFC Dowker space in <math>\aleph_{\omega+1}</math>: an application of PCF theory to topology |journal=[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society|Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.]] |publisher=American Mathematical Society |volume=126 |number=8 |pages=2459–2465 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-98-04884-9 |url=https://www.ams.org/proc/1998-126-08/S0002-9939-98-04884-9/S0002-9939-98-04884-9.pdf |accessdate=March 29, 2015}}</ref>
